title: Two developers, one measure
seo: Power BI PBIP and TMDL Git merge conflict exercise: resolve a conflict in a semantic model, run Best Practice Analyzer, and write the pull request.
summary: You and Sam changed the same measure in the shared semantic model on different branches. Git can't merge it. Resolve it without losing either change.

verified.context: PBIP/TMDL/PBIR project format (Microsoft Learn, 2026-09-23); Tabular Editor 2 BPA

story: The shared model from Sprint 05 now lives in Git as a PBIP project. Every change goes through a pull request reviewed by someone else before Elena deploys it.
impact: A careless merge silently drops someone's change, or renames a measure that twenty visuals still reference, and nobody notices until a report shows blanks in production. Merging well is what makes team development safe.

body: Hey, my branch renames Net Sales to Net Revenue (Finance asked for the wording after the consolidation) and adds Net Revenue %. Yours excludes Staff and adds Net Sales LY, right? Git says conflict in _Measures.tmdl. Can you sort it out? I'm in workshops all afternoon. Just take mine if in doubt 😅

messages.subject: Review checklist for the release train
body:
- Both changes kept unless one is wrong.
- No broken references in measures or in report visuals.
- BPA: no new errors (severity 3); warnings explained.
- PR description: what changed, why, how it was tested, risk, rollback.

messages.subject: Net Revenue name
body: Just so you know: in the KPI dictionary "Net Revenue (ledger)" is the Finance measure. I asked Sam to rename the order-based one, but I didn't mean to call it plain "Net Revenue"! Can we make sure the names don't clash?

evidence.title: git_log.txt
evidence.desc: Branch graph, the failed merge, and where the report uses the measure.

tasks: Work out what each branch changed relative to the common ancestor (a three-way comparison, not two files side by side).
Resolve the conflict so both intentions survive, and so no measure or visual references a name that no longer exists.
Validate: the file must open in Power BI Desktop (or parse in Tabular Editor), every measure must evaluate, and BPA must show no new errors.
Commit with a meaningful message and write the pull request description, including risk and rollback.

deliverables.t: List of every reference you had to update (measures and report visuals)
BPA result after the merge, with each remaining warning explained

hints: Diff base→ours and base→theirs separately. List each change as a sentence ("ours: Net Sales now excludes Staff"). The conflict is only where both sentences touch the same lines.

Both branches changed the same measure: one changed its expression, the other its name and format. The resolved measure needs one name, one expression and one format. Then look for everything that still says [Net Sales]: a measure on your branch and three visuals in the report.
Before you pick the new name, read Nina's email and the KPI dictionary from Sprint 05. What should the order-based measure be called so it can never be confused with the ledger one?

rubric.good: Resolved file keeps the Staff exclusion, the LY measure and the % measure, uses one agreed name everywhere, has no conflict markers and evaluates.
Finds and updates every reference: the LY measure, the % measure and the three report visuals (or keeps the old name and explains why).
Opens the project, refreshes, compares values before and after, runs BPA and explains remaining warnings.
PR description says what, why, how tested, risk and rollback; Sam and Nina know the final name.
Merge commit message is meaningful; no unrelated files (localSettings.json, cache.abf) committed.

retro: Why did Git produce a conflict here when it merged other files automatically?
What working agreement would make this conflict less likely next time?
How do renames interact with reports that reference measures by name?
